docs.title: Welcome to the Data Dictionary Hub
docs.text:
Welcome to the central documentation platform for our project's database.

This platform is designed to make our data structure transparent, accessible, and easy to understand for everyone involved in the project—whether you are a developer, a data analyst, or a domain expert.

docs.title: Our Objectives
docs.text:
The main goals of this data dictionary are:

  • Single Source of Truth: Provide a reliable and standardized reference for all database entities, their attributes, and relationships.
  • Accessibility: Offer a simple, fast, and easily shareable web interface. No complex software installations or database credentials are required to understand our data.
  • Clarity & Context: Go beyond just "data types". Here you will find business definitions, constraints, example values, and specific rules (e.g., geographical data handling) for every single column.
  • Collaborative Maintenance: Empower non-technical team members to keep the documentation alive and updated through a simplified workflow.

docs.title: How to Navigate
docs.text:
Finding the information you need is quick and straightforward:

  1. Search Bar: Use the powerful search bar at the top of the page. It instantly looks through table names, column definitions, and comments.
  2. Interactive Schema: Start with the Schema Overview (ER) to get a bird's-eye view of how different tables relate to each other.
  3. Table Details: Browse the sidebar navigation menu to dive deep into specific domains and tables. Each page provides an exhaustive breakdown of the selected table.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
Documentation is only useful if it stays up to date. We built this platform so that anyone can contribute, no coding required.

!!! info "Updating the Dictionary via Excel"

You don't need to know Markdown or Git to help out! We manage updates via a simple **Excel template**.

If you need to define a new table or update an existing description, you just need to fill out a spreadsheet containing columns like *Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.*

The technical team will automatically convert your Excel sheet into these web pages. Please read the [Contribution Guidelines](guidelines.md) for more details.

If you find any discrepancies or have questions about specific data entities, please reach out to the database administration team.

docs.title: Contribution Guidelines
docs.text:
Thank you for helping us keep the Data Dictionary accurate and up-to-date!

Good documentation is a team effort. You do not need to be a developer, know how to write code, or understand Git to contribute to this project. All content updates are managed through a simple spreadsheet.

docs.title: The Workflow
docs.text:
Updating the dictionary takes just three simple steps:

  1. Download the template: Grab the latest version of the Data Dictionary Excel template from our shared team folder.
  2. Fill in the data: Add or update the rows corresponding to the database tables and columns you are documenting.
  3. Submit for publishing: Send the updated Excel file to the technical team. We will run an automated process to convert your spreadsheet into the web pages you see here.

docs.title: How to fill out the Excel template
docs.text:
Each sheet in the Excel file represents a single database table. For every column in that table, please provide the following details:

  • Column: The exact technical name of the field in the database (e.g., user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: The format of the data (e.g., VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): A clear, business-friendly description of what the column represents. Please fill out both the Italian and English columns to support our bilingual platform.
  • Example value: A realistic example of the data to help others understand the format (e.g., john.doe@email.com or POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Note any database rules, such as PK (Primary Key), FK (Foreign Key), or NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specify if the field contains spatial data (e.g., Yes - EPSG:4326 or No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Any extra context, business logic, or warnings regarding how this data should be used or interpreted.

!!! warning "Keep Formatting Simple" Please avoid using complex Excel formatting like merged cells, custom cell colors, or multiple lines inside a single cell. Plain text ensures the smoothest conversion to the web platform!

docs.title: Submitting Your Changes
docs.text:
Once your Excel file is ready and reviewed:

  • Upload the new version to the designated shared drive.
  • Notify the database administration team via email or our internal chat.
  • The team will process the file, and your changes will be live on the Data Dictionary within a few minutes!

docs.title: Schema overview
docs.text:
The public schema is organised around three groups of tables:

  1. Enterprises: the owned, located units that can be damaged (buildings, farms, businesses, network systems).
  2. Components: the physical or economic elements that belong to an enterprise (crops, machinery, staff, road segments, and so on).
  3. Assessment: events, surveys and the damage records they produce.

Enterprises and components both use table-per-subtype inheritance: a sub-type table shares the primary key of its parent, so a row is joined to its parent with child.id = parent.id.

The schema is shown in three diagrams to keep each one readable.

docs.title: Table: added_block
docs.text: Description (EN): This table represents added blocks of buildings. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the component table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent component record.

Comments id BIGINT Unique identifier for the added block 42 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing component.id position VARCHAR [...] EXTERNAL - No [...] vertical_mat VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] horizontal_mat VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] n_floor BIGINT Number of floors of the added block 2 - No [...] total_height BIGINT Total height of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] floor_surface BIGINT Total floor surface of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] floor_height BIGINT Total floor height of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] function VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] previous_survey VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...]

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): component. The added_block table is a specialized extension of the component table.
  • Belongs to: enterprise (A component sub-type is linked to one enterprise)
  • Has many: damage (A component sub-type can be affected by multiple damage over time)

!!! tip "Where is the rest of the data?" To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or ownership details of a added_block, you must join this table with the component record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all added blocks, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent component entity:

SELECT 
    ab.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    added_block ab
JOIN 
    component c ON ab.id = c.id
WHERE 
    c.component_kind  = 'ADDED_BLOCK';

docs.title: Table: building
docs.text: Description: This table stores the structural, economic, and physical characteristics of buildings, including construction details, material types, and spatial dimensions. Categorical attributes are managed via CHECK constraints directly within the table definition. It inherits characteristics of the more generic entity Enterprise.

docs.title: Column structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Building unique identifier 3 PK, FK No Primay key that acts as external one for enterprise.id

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): enterprise. The building table is an extension of the enterprise table.
  • Note: To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or VAT of a building, you must look at the enterprise record with the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve the full details of a building by joining its specific structural data with its general enterprise data (such as name and town):

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    b.*
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

docs.title: Benvenuto nell'Hub del Dizionario Dati
docs.text:
Benvenuto nella piattaforma centrale di documentazione per il database del nostro progetto.

Questa piattaforma è progettata per rendere la nostra struttura dati trasparente, accessibile e facile da capire per tutte le persone coinvolte nel progetto, che tu sia uno sviluppatore, un data analyst o un esperto del settore.

docs.title: I Nostri Obiettivi
docs.text:
Gli scopi principali di questo dizionario dati sono:

  • Unica Fonte di Verità: Fornire un riferimento affidabile e standardizzato per tutte le entità del database, i loro attributi e le loro relazioni.
  • Accessibilità: Offrire un'interfaccia web semplice, veloce e facilmente condivisibile. Non sono necessarie installazioni di software complessi o credenziali del database per comprendere i nostri dati.
  • Chiarezza e Contesto: Andare oltre i semplici "tipi di dato". Qui troverai definizioni di business, vincoli, valori di esempio e regole specifiche (es. gestione dei dati geografici) per ogni singola colonna.
  • Manutenzione Collaborativa: Permettere ai membri del team non tecnici di mantenere viva e aggiornata la documentazione attraverso un flusso di lavoro semplificato.

docs.title: Come Navigare
docs.text:
Trovare le informazioni di cui hai bisogno è rapido e intuitivo:

  1. Barra di Ricerca: Usa la potente barra di ricerca in cima alla pagina. Cerca istantaneamente tra i nomi delle tabelle, le definizioni delle colonne e i commenti.
  2. Schema Interattivo: Inizia dalla Panoramica Schema (ER) per avere una visione d'insieme di come le diverse tabelle si relazionano tra loro.
  3. Dettagli Tabelle: Esplora il menu di navigazione laterale per approfondire domini e tabelle specifiche. Ogni pagina fornisce un'analisi esauriente della tabella selezionata.

docs.title: Come Contribuire
docs.text:
La documentazione è utile solo se rimane aggiornata. Abbiamo costruito questa piattaforma in modo che chiunque possa contribuire, senza dover scrivere codice.

!!! info "Aggiornare il Dizionario tramite Excel" Non è necessario conoscere Markdown o Git per dare una mano! Gestiamo gli aggiornamenti tramite un semplice template Excel. 

Se devi definire una nuova tabella o aggiornare una descrizione esistente, ti basterà compilare un foglio di calcolo contenente colonne come *Data type, Definition, Example value, ecc.*

Il team tecnico convertirà automaticamente il tuo foglio Excel in queste pagine web. Ti preghiamo di leggere le [Linee Guida per Contribuire](guidelines.md) per maggiori dettagli.

Se riscontri delle discrepanze o hai domande su specifiche entità di dati, ti preghiamo di contattare il team di amministrazione del database.

docs.title: Linee Guida per Contribuire
docs.text:
Grazie per aiutarci a mantenere il Dizionario Dati accurato e aggiornato!

Una buona documentazione è un lavoro di squadra. Non è necessario essere sviluppatori, saper programmare o conoscere Git per contribuire a questo progetto. Tutti gli aggiornamenti dei contenuti sono gestiti tramite un semplice foglio di calcolo.

docs.title: Il Flusso di Lavoro
docs.text:
Aggiornare il dizionario richiede solo tre semplici passaggi:

  1. Scarica il Template: Recupera l'ultima versione del template Excel del Dizionario Dati dalla nostra cartella condivisa del team.
  2. Compila i Dati: Aggiungi o aggiorna le righe corrispondenti alle tabelle e alle colonne del database che stai documentando.
  3. Invia per la Pubblicazione: Invia il file Excel aggiornato al team tecnico. Eseguiremo un processo automatico per convertire il tuo foglio di calcolo nelle pagine web che vedi qui.

docs.title: Come Compilare il Template Excel
docs.text:
Ogni foglio nel file Excel rappresenta una singola tabella del database. Per ogni colonna in quella tabella, fornisci i seguenti dettagli:

  • Column: Il nome tecnico esatto del campo nel database (es. user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: Il formato dei dati (es. VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): Una descrizione chiara e comprensibile di cosa rappresenta la colonna. Ti preghiamo di compilare sia la colonna italiana che quella inglese per supportare la nostra piattaforma multilingua.
  • Example value: Un esempio realistico del dato per aiutare gli altri a capirne il formato (es. mario.rossi@email.com o POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Annota eventuali regole del database, come PK (Primary Key/Chiave Primaria), FK (Foreign Key/Chiave Esterna), o NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specifica se il campo contiene dati spaziali (es. Sì - EPSG:4326 o No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Qualsiasi contesto aggiuntivo, logica di business o avvertenza su come questo dato dovrebbe essere utilizzato o interpretato.

!!! warning "Mantieni la Formattazione Semplice" Ti preghiamo di evitare l'uso di formattazioni complesse in Excel, come celle unite, colori personalizzati o più righe all'interno di una singola cella. Il testo semplice garantisce una conversione senza intoppi sulla piattaforma web!

docs.title: Inviare le Modifiche
docs.text:
Una volta che il tuo file Excel è pronto e revisionato:

  • Carica la nuova versione nel drive condiviso designato.
  • Avvisa il team di amministrazione del database tramite email o la nostra chat interna.
  • Il team elaborerà il file e le tue modifiche saranno online sul Dizionario Dati in pochi minuti!

    b.n_floors,
    b.construction_cost,

FROM 
    enterprise

docs.title: Welcome to the Data Dictionary Hub
docs.text:
Welcome to the central documentation platform for our project's database.

This platform is designed to make our data structure transparent, accessible, and easy to understand for everyone involved in the project—whether you are a developer, a data analyst, or a domain expert.

docs.title: Our Objectives
docs.text:
The main goals of this data dictionary are:

  • Single Source of Truth: Provide a reliable and standardized reference for all database entities, their attributes, and relationships.
  • Accessibility: Offer a simple, fast, and easily shareable web interface. No complex software installations or database credentials are required to understand our data.
  • Clarity & Context: Go beyond just "data types". Here you will find business definitions, constraints, example values, and specific rules (e.g., geographical data handling) for every single column.
  • Collaborative Maintenance: Empower non-technical team members to keep the documentation alive and updated through a simplified workflow.

docs.title: How to Navigate
docs.text:
Finding the information you need is quick and straightforward:

  1. Search Bar: Use the powerful search bar at the top of the page. It instantly looks through table names, column definitions, and comments.
  2. Interactive Schema: Start with the Schema Overview (ER) to get a bird's-eye view of how different tables relate to each other.
  3. Table Details: Browse the sidebar navigation menu to dive deep into specific domains and tables. Each page provides an exhaustive breakdown of the selected table.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
Documentation is only useful if it stays up to date. We built this platform so that anyone can contribute, no coding required.

!!! info "Updating the Dictionary via Excel"

You don't need to know Markdown or Git to help out! We manage updates via a simple **Excel template**.

If you need to define a new table or update an existing description, you just need to fill out a spreadsheet containing columns like *Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.*

The technical team will automatically convert your Excel sheet into these web pages. Please read the [Contribution Guidelines](guidelines.md) for more details.

If you find any discrepancies or have questions about specific data entities, please reach out to the database administration team.

docs.title: Contribution Guidelines
docs.text:
Thank you for helping us keep the Data Dictionary accurate and up-to-date!

Good documentation is a team effort. You do not need to be a developer, know how to write code, or understand Git to contribute to this project. All content updates are managed through a simple spreadsheet.

docs.title: The Workflow
docs.text:
Updating the dictionary takes just three simple steps:

  1. Download the template: Grab the latest version of the Data Dictionary Excel template from our shared team folder.
  2. Fill in the data: Add or update the rows corresponding to the database tables and columns you are documenting.
  3. Submit for publishing: Send the updated Excel file to the technical team. We will run an automated process to convert your spreadsheet into the web pages you see here.

docs.title: How to fill out the Excel template
docs.text:
Each sheet in the Excel file represents a single database table. For every column in that table, please provide the following details:

  • Column: The exact technical name of the field in the database (e.g., user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: The format of the data (e.g., VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): A clear, business-friendly description of what the column represents. Please fill out both the Italian and English columns to support our bilingual platform.
  • Example value: A realistic example of the data to help others understand the format (e.g., john.doe@email.com or POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Note any database rules, such as PK (Primary Key), FK (Foreign Key), or NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specify if the field contains spatial data (e.g., Yes - EPSG:4326 or No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Any extra context, business logic, or warnings regarding how this data should be used or interpreted.

!!! warning "Keep Formatting Simple" Please avoid using complex Excel formatting like merged cells, custom cell colors, or multiple lines inside a single cell. Plain text ensures the smoothest conversion to the web platform!

docs.title: Submitting Your Changes
docs.text:
Once your Excel file is ready and reviewed:

  • Upload the new version to the designated shared drive.
  • Notify the database administration team via email or our internal chat.
  • The team will process the file, and your changes will be live on the Data Dictionary within a few minutes!

docs.title: Schema overview
docs.text:
The public schema is organised around three groups of tables:

  1. Enterprises: the owned, located units that can be damaged (buildings, farms, businesses, network systems).
  2. Components: the physical or economic elements that belong to an enterprise (crops, machinery, staff, road segments, and so on).
  3. Assessment: events, surveys and the damage records they produce.

Enterprises and components both use table-per-subtype inheritance: a sub-type table shares the primary key of its parent, so a row is joined to its parent with child.id = parent.id.

The schema is shown in three diagrams to keep each one readable.

It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent enterprise record.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Unique identifier for the farm 42 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing enterprise.id

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): enterprise. The farm table is a specialized extension of the enterprise table.
  • Contains: While not linked directly via a farm_id, a farm owns agricultural assets through the enterprise_id column in the component table. These components often include specialized agricultural sub-types such as:
    • agriculture_product and its sub-types crop and stored
    • livestock
    • fixed_asset and its sub-types (e.g. machinery such as tractors)

!!! tip "Where is the rest of the data?" To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or other details of a farm, you must join this table with the enterprise record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all farms, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent enterprise entity:

SELECT 
    f.id, 
    e.name, 
    e.town, 
    ST_AsText(e.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    farm f
JOIN 
    enterprise e ON f.id = e.id
WHERE 
    e.type = 'FARM';

docs.title: Markdown Template Standards
docs.text: This document defines standard conventions for Markdown templates.

docs.title: Headings
docs.text:
• Use # for top-level headings.
  • Use ## for second-level headings and so on.
  • Keep heading text concise and descriptive.

docs.title: Paragraphs
docs.text:
• Separate paragraphs with a blank line.
  • Avoid long lines by wrapping text at around 80 characters.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
• Use - or * for unordered lists.
  • Use numbers with periods for ordered lists.
  • Indent nested list items by two spaces.

docs.title: Code Blocks
docs.text:
• Use fenced code blocks with language identifiers:

```python
print('Hello world')
```

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
• Use a header row and separator row.
  • Align columns with spaces for readability.

Example:

Column Description Name The item name Value The item value

docs.title: Links and References
docs.text:
• Use relative links for internal documentation.
  • Use full URLs for external references.

docs.title: Emphasis
docs.text:
• Use **bold** for strong emphasis.
  • Use *italic* for emphasis.
  • Use backticks for inline code.

• Inherits from (Sub-type of): network_system. The electrical_system table is a specialized extension of the network_system table.
  • Contains: While not linked directly via a transport_system_id, a transport system owns infrastructural assets through the enterprise_id column in the component table. These components often include specialized sub-types such as:
    • transport_network_component

!!! tip "Where is the rest of the data?" To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or ownership details of a network system, you must join this table with the enterprise record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all electrical systems, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent network_system - enterprise entity:

```sql SELECT tr.id, e.name, e.town, ST_AsText(e.geometry) as coordinates FROM transport_system tr JOIN enterprise e ON tr.id = e.id WHERE e.type = 'TRANSPORT';
